stories.notes: Empty acceptance criteria with null spec for a complex multi-market (GO, UP, MX) live preview feature. openspec should elaborate AC, propose market-specific story splits, and add technical depth around real-time rendering, iframe sandboxing, and state sync. speckit then hardens with testability criteria, security checks (XSS, iframe sandbox policies), and edge cases (offline, concurrent edits, large content).

agentContributions.notes: Openspec provided empty acceptance criteria ('context' note only). I built the full AC set from the story title 'Live Preview of Content in CMS' and the listed technical files. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1 establishes the core live-preview observable behavior with a 5-second tolerance; (2) AC-2 through AC-6 map each listed file to a testable outcome; (3) AC-7 and AC-10 cover the graceful-degradation path when Live Preview is disabled/unconfigured — critical for production; (4) AC-8 and AC-9 handle error/edge cases (connection loss, malformed data); (5) AC-11 addresses rapid-update debouncing/coalescing; (6) AC-12 covers partial-data handling for the contentCard interface; (7) AC-13 covers stale-data cleanup when the author leaves the editor; (8) AC-14 ensures subscription cleanup on unmount. I could not inspect file contents to verify existing interfaces or patterns; if the actual code structure differs significantly, some criteria may need adjustment.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: OpenSpec produced no meaningful elaboration — only a 'context' note with no AC refinement, no market-specific story splits, and no technical depth around real-time rendering, iframe sandboxing, or state sync as the coordinator notes requested. Speckit compensated by building the entire AC set from scratch (14 criteria covering core behavior, error/edge cases, degradation, debouncing, cleanup), but this inverts the intended pipeline: Speckit should harden OpenSpec's output, not replace it. Speckit also flagged it could not inspect file contents, so criteria may not match actual code structure. The collaborative spec work did not function as designed — one agent added no value while the other carried the full load.
